proposal_topic_title: Non-Hermitian Photonic Methods for Medical-Imaging Hardware
proposal_topic_intro:
Non-Hermitian optical systems exhibit exotic gain-loss dynamics that enable exceptional-point sensing with sensitivity far beyond conventional limits. PT-symmetric microrings and topological photonic superlattices offer a new hardware substrate for the active optical components inside next-generation medical imaging instruments.

Combining these photonic advances with terahertz frequency-modulated continuous-wave sensing could yield compact, high-contrast scanners suitable for bedside or point-of-care deployment. The cloud-based image-analysis layer then provides scalable post-processing without requiring specialist on-site compute.

participating_pis.research_summary: Alpha leads Lab-Alpha, a group combining applied photonics, medical imaging, and algebraic geometry. Recent work spans frequency-modulated continuous-wave terahertz systems for aerospace nondestructive testing, a privacy-preserving cloud framework for clinical image analysis, and morphism dimensions in 3-Calabi-Yau categories.

Beta leads Lab-Beta, focused on AI-driven eldercare and causal machine learning. The lab built an AIoT system achieving >99% activity-inference accuracy for dementia monitoring in smart homes, and developed a causal variable discovery framework for multi-label data with minimal-redundancy feature selection.

Gamma leads Lab-Gamma, specialising in spiking neural networks and LLM-guided algorithm selection. The lab produced a biologically inspired SNN model for precise sound localisation in noisy environments, a multi-task speaker-verification framework, and pioneered LLM-evolutionary algorithm selection.

Delta leads Lab-Delta, working at the intersection of optical physics and theoretical computer science. Current projects include PT-symmetric microring analysis for coherent perfect absorption, multi-mode interference in non-Hermitian optical systems, and topological photonics superlattice tunability.
